body.target_estimand: \(\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y(a)]=\theta(a)\), jointly for \(a\in J\) and every full-data witness \(P^{\mathrm F}\) of \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \(\texttt{ass:potential-mean-continuity}\)

sampling_model.design: Observational independent sampling from an observed marginal law \(P\in\mathcal M\); causal interpretation is uniform over every full-data extension \(P^{\mathrm F}\) witnessing membership, including the continuous conditional potential-outcome mean version required for exact-dose identification.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A fixed number of folds and explicit boundary-corrected local-polynomial learners with bandwidth \(n^{-1/(2s)}\) are used for \(p,g,m,r\) on the instrumental fixed-radius subclass. Their product bias, local centered empirical perturbation, variance-normalization error, and clock error must satisfy \(\mathsf G_n\); the pooled validation-fold pseudo-outcomes then define one Grenander primitive.
sampling_model.overlap: The conditional density \(g(a\mid w)\) is bounded above and away from zero.
sampling_model.treatment: Continuous dose \(A_i\in[0,1]\), with inference restricted to \(J=[\delta,1-\delta]\).
sampling_model.units: \(O_i=(W_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with compact covariates and bounded outcomes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The limiting distribution is the integral of the difference of the squared constrained and unconstrained slope processes.
We study the extremal behavior of the stationary argmax process on increasing intervals.
A suitably standardized supremum of the Grenander-type estimation error converges to a standard Gumbel random variable.
The confidence intervals concern the continuous treatment effect curve at a fixed point and invert a likelihood-ratio-type test.
The paper provides general conditions for consistency and pointwise convergence of generalized Grenander-type estimators.
Approximation results for the supremum of an empirical process yield asymptotically valid uniform confidence bands.
The paper develops a bootstrap procedure for constructing uniform confidence bands from weighted local-linear estimation.

body.tldr: Pointwise causal-isotonic likelihood-ratio inference is available, but scanning a whole dose-response profile changes calibration because approximately \(n^{1/3}\) strongly dependent Brownian--GCM LR opportunities are encountered. For observed laws admitting a causal full-data extension under an explicit maintained continuous-version convention, the project works on a nonempty instrumental fixed-radius \(C^s\) subclass, derives the sharp Palm-cluster excursion intensity, additive tail ratio, constructive centering, and Poisson law of the canonical LR field under a fully specified cutoff, mesh, runs rule, padding scheme, and block regime, and defines centering and scale only on \(T\ge T_0\). A separate quantitative theorem verifies the product-bias, local empirical, variance-normalization, and clock errors needed at the moving Gumbel level before transferring the result to a pooled cross-fitted AIPW Grenander primitive and constructing simultaneous curve and threshold-crossing confidence sets for nurse-hours and readmission.

project_justification.gap: The literature contains the universal fixed-point LR law, extreme-value theory for the Brownian-parabolic argmax and Grenander slope error, pointwise causal LR intervals, and smoothing-based Gaussian bands. It does not contain the high-excursion and cluster law of the Brownian--GCM LR energy field or an extreme-scale transfer for a cross-fitted causal primitive.
project_justification.niche: This leaves exact joint calibration of the established unsmoothed causal-isotonic profile procedure without a theorem, even though the entire scientific profile rather than one prespecified dose is routinely inspected.
project_justification.fill: Exact-dose causal interpretation is obtained under an explicitly maintained jointly measurable continuous conditional-potential-mean version convention, separate from the excursion theory. The canonical theorem fixes the contact radius, truncation and padding radius, mesh, runs rule, Palm root event, exact cluster intensity, expansion class, block regime, and eventual thresholds \(u_0\) and \(T_0\). On the instrumental global fixed-radius \(C^s\) subclass, a separate quantitative result derives nuisance rates and verifies the exact product-bias, local empirical, variance-normalization, and clock thresholds needed for Gumbel-scale transfer. The remaining statistical results establish the observed-law spatial time change, feasible eventual-regime calibration, joint profile coverage, and threshold-crossing inversion; an explicit full-data witness proves nonemptiness.

body.related_work: Banerjee and Wellner (2001) supply the fixed-point Brownian--GCM LR functional; Theorem 1 strictly tightens that one-location result to the explicitly defined Palm intensity and growing-domain excursions on \(T\ge T_0\). Hooghiemstra and Lopuhaä (1998) and Durot, Kulikov, and Lopuhaä (2012) inform the extreme-value architecture through the Brownian-parabolic argmax and Grenander slope error, but their statistics do not encode constrained-versus-unconstrained GCM projection energy. Hsing, Hüsler, and Leadbetter (1988) supplies the cluster point-process framework used with the fixed contact cutoff, mesh, runs rule, and Palm root event. Westling and Carone (2020) and Westling, Gilbert, and Carone (2020) supply generalized Grenander and causal-isotonic primitives, consistency, and pointwise limits; the full-data marginal bookkeeping and exact-dose continuous conditional-potential-mean version convention are maintained in this core rather than attributed to those papers. Doss (2026) supplies the fixed-dose doubly robust LR construction and product-remainder motivation; Theorem 2 strictly tightens that fixed-dose result to a continuum maximum only on the explicitly strengthened subclass. Takatsu and Westling (2025) provide neighboring local-linear Gaussian bands and verify bounded-outcome and uniform empirical-process conditions, but they do not assume the common global fixed-radius \(C^s\) conditions on \(p,g,m,r\) used here. Ai, Huang, and Zhang (2026) provide bootstrap smoothing bands and are a methodological alternative rather than a dominance target. A public Doss--VandenBerg 2026 abstract and slides advertise multiscale adaptive shape-constrained simultaneous bands and already analyze nurse staffing, but no public archival theorem text was available for audit; no claim of narrower width, tuning freedom, adaptation superiority, or dominance over that work is made.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The deterministic Cameron--Martin scaling and the plateau witness with LR energy one and action \(9/8\) are diagnostics only. They do not establish the probabilistic tail rate, the additive ratio, the cluster intensity, or the Poisson limit. The early kill test must reproduce this witness and stable localization on oracle PAVA grids before the causal proof is developed; a verified failure of localization or additive-ratio scaling calls for an analytic counterexample and termination of this spine.
body.honest_scope: The sharp canonical excursion theorem, including the Palm-root intensity expansion, constructive \(o(1)\) centering, and cluster law in the stated block regime, is open and load-bearing. Its expansion defines \(b(T)\), positive \(a(T)\), marked processes, simulations, and feasible critical values only on \(T\ge T_0\). Exact-dose causal identification additionally maintains a novel jointly measurable continuous conditional-potential-mean version convention over every full-data extension witnessing model membership; consistency, exchangeability, overlap, and the smooth observed regression version then identify that version with \(m\). The common global fixed-radius \(C^s\) conditions on \(p,g,m,r\), the two-sided covariate-density bound, and the explicit learner choice are instrumental strengthened restrictions, not assumptions attributed to Takatsu and Westling (2025). The separate threshold theorem must derive \(n^{5/6}(\log n)^{3/2}\mathfrak B_n=o_P(1)\), \(\sqrt{\log n}\,\mathfrak R_n=o_P(1)\), \((\log n)\mathfrak K_n=o_P(1)\), and relative clock consistency before causal LR transfer is available. The explicit uniform-design linear-response witness establishes nonemptiness. The model excludes flat stretches, vanishing overlap, growing confounder dimension, shrinking interior buffers, and mixed-smoothness regimes. The proposal claims asymptotically exact joint calibration for this LR profile, not optimal width, global tuning freedom, or superiority to Gaussian multiscale bands. Under homogeneous \(f\), \(\theta'\), and \(\kappa\), it reduces to a deterministic-horizon canonical maximum and at one dose to the Banerjee--Wellner law.
